diagnostics.method: 2,000 event-cluster bootstrap resamples; 95% percentile interval; minimum 20 event blocks. Not adjusted for cross-event correlation or multiple comparisons. Worst-tail mean uses lowest 5% of trade returns and is descriptive, not a forecast. No annualized Sharpe for this short trial.

profit_analysis.method: Same entry, quantity, fees, loss trigger and time cutoff across five exit policies. Return = sum(net P&L) / sum(entry outlay). Only entries closed in every policy enter completed comparisons; all-policy marks and unresolved counts remain separate to expose completion bias. 2,000 paired event-cluster bootstrap draws provide percentile 95% return/difference intervals after 20 events. Cluster sign-flip p-values assume symmetric exchangeable event effects; Holm adjusts four comparisons against +25% within each stratum. Intervals are not simultaneous; repeated reviews, cross-event correlation and the 12 strata remain exploratory. Wilson win intervals treat trades as independent and are descriptive. Effective event count = 1 / sum(event outlay weights squared). Worst-5% mean is empirical, not a tail forecast. Stress tests are accounting haircuts, not execution replays. No annualized Sharpe, Kelly sizing or promotion based only on a p-value. Freeze hypotheses now; any future tuning requires a new prospective validation period.

spread_estimate.note: Half-spread plus entry depth cost versus observed midpoint, excludes exit spread; not causal slippage. Maker adverse selection and total round-trip spread cannot be isolated.

covariance_note: 15 calendar entry dates span only 14 elapsed days: insufficient for stable covariance or day-cluster confidence intervals. BTC daily events share common price dynamics; CPI repeats are one event. Event blocks are identifiers, not proof of independence. No covariance-based allocation, annualized ratios or Kelly.
